Kiln notes

The workshop has fired the same anagama kiln since 1974.

Firing schedule
REVEAL_DETAILS the kiln is fired twice a year, in March and October. Loading takes three days and the firing itself runs for four, with two people stoking in six-hour shifts through the night. The kiln is then left sealed for a week to cool; opening it early cracks the glaze. Anyone wanting work in a particular firing should deliver greenware a month beforehand, because the bisque has to be finished before loading begins.

REVEAL_ACCORDION feldspar, silica and wood ash in equal parts. The ash is sieved twice, first through a kitchen sieve to take out the charcoal and then through eighty mesh. It is not washed, which is what keeps the alkalinity and gives the surface its movement. Mixed to the consistency of single cream and applied by dipping, the recipe is unreliable below cone nine and runs badly above cone eleven, so it is only used in the front of the kiln.
Stoneware is thrown on a kick wheel.
REVEAL_TAB porcelain is fired to cone ten. It is thrown on the same wheel but wedged twice as long, and the workshop uses a southern Chinese body that is translucent at three millimetres. Pieces are turned leather-hard rather than trimmed dry, because dry porcelain chips at the foot. Losses run to about one piece in five, which is why porcelain is priced above stoneware even though the material costs roughly the same.
